cohort_context: Hudson Technologies is the largest US refrigerant reclaimer (NAICS 325120 Industrial Gas Manufacturing). FY24 10-K filed 2025-03-12. AIRO-signature mechanical hit (the strings 'material weakness' and 'stock for services' both appear in the 10-K) is a known FALSE POSITIVE: the 'material weakness' hit is boilerplate from the auditor's standard ICFR-risk paragraph, and 'stock for services' is a generic line item on the equity rollforward (not a distress-financing event). The real bear thesis is fundamental: the HFC phase-down under the AIM Act compresses commodity refrigerant pricing, the DLA prime contract (15% of revenue) expires July 2026, and FY24 inventory was written down (from $154.5M to $96.2M). HDSN's forward 12-month return was -37.6% but for fundamentals, not for disclosure-quality reasons. Plan tests whether multi-source aggregation correctly DE-EMITS this name because operational claims are independently corroborated (real EPA-permitted reclamation facilities, real DLA federal contract, real AHRI-certified lab, real patents), rather than emitting on the false-positive AIRO triggers.

claims.extraction_notes: financial_distress is CANONICAL (primary: claim_evolution + sec_filings). This claim is the CONTRADICTION of the AIRO mechanical screen — applying heuristic H10 (distress-cluster fingerprints require >=2-3 markers within 6 months) HDSN does NOT cluster: no reverse split, no ATM, no auditor qualifier, no going-concern, no layoffs, no restatement. Per the H10 discipline, I am DELIBERATELY NOT firing distress heuristics on the AIRO-screen boilerplate keyword hit. sec_filings.list_filings_by_form is mapped to test whether ANY of the canonical distress-marker form types (NT 10-Q/K = late filing; S-3/424B5 = ATM shelf usage) actually appear; absence = corroboration of non-distress.
